source_tradition: The Monroe Institute / Gateway Experience — Wave III Freedom
policy: Technique descriptions are mapped separately from claimed outcomes.
Gateway references to nonphysical energy or a second body remain program/framework language and are not imported into Nova ontology.
A technique may target an NC transition without being equivalent to that transition.
Where Gateway explicitly says an exercise does not necessarily imply actual separation, the crosswalk preserves that distinction.

concepts.label: Freedom #1 — Liftoff
concepts.notes: Floating-perspective exercise in Focus 10; manual explicitly says this does not necessarily imply actual physical-body separation.

concepts.label: Freedom #3 — Vectors
concepts.notes: Uses body-referenced clock positions to train directional control and repeatable movement/orientation.

concepts.label: Freedom #6 — First-Stage Separation
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: First-Stage Separation
concepts.notes: Umbrella exercise teaching five methods described as dissociation/separation methods.

concepts.label: First-Stage Separation — Log-rolling
concepts.notes: Deliberate rotation around a head-to-feet axis, followed by allowing the rotation and moving outward.

concepts.label: First-Stage Separation — Pole
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: Pole method
concepts.notes: Sequentially moves the described second-body representation out head-first while feet remain the pivot until intended full separation.

concepts.label: First-Stage Separation — Backing away
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: Backing away
concepts.notes: Imagined/perceived backward movement away from the physical body before directional movement.

concepts.label: First-Stage Separation — Flowing
concepts.notes: Describes sending nonphysical-energy imagery out through the head as cloud/fog/spray before re-forming into a body-like shape.

concepts.label: First-Stage Separation — Floating
concepts.notes: Uses emotional association with floating/soaring to support the intended separation process.

mappings.basis: Liftoff trains a floating/rising perspective while awareness is experienced as displaced relative to the physical body; Nova Flottement models the corresponding light/suspended/rising sensation.
mappings.warning: Gateway explicitly states that Liftoff does not necessarily imply actual separation.

mappings.basis: The manual distinguishes the perspective/movement exercise from necessary actual separation; Nova Décrochage is the transition itself rather than a floating cue or rehearsal.
mappings.warning: Do not count Liftoff practice as a reported Décrochage event.

mappings.basis: Vectors trains choosing and reproducing directional reference points and controlled movement; Nova Orientation is the action of selecting a direction, target or intentional reference.
mappings.warning: Gateway's nonphysical-space theory is not required for the operational mapping.

mappings.basis: Freedom #6 explicitly teaches methods intended to move from ordinary bodily localization into a separated/out-of-phase condition; Nova Décrochage is the modeled transition rather than the destination.
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: First-Stage Separation
mappings.warning: Training objective and actually reported transition remain separate data fields.

mappings.basis: Both procedures deliberately use/amplify axial rotation as a separation method rather than treating rotation as a merely spontaneous sensation.
mappings.warning: Gateway's second-body/nonphysical-energy explanation remains source framing.

mappings.basis: The pole procedure explicitly stages a head/shoulders/chest/waist/legs progression while the feet remain the last contact point, closely resembling Nova's partial-exit transition before complete separation.
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: Pole method
mappings.warning: The technique sequence is not evidence that all spontaneous partial exits follow this order.

mappings.basis: Backing away converts a simple directional intention into a separation maneuver; Nova Intention de séparation explicitly models simple directed movement-away intent and Décrochage the transition it may precede/facilitate.
source_basis: Gateway Experience Manual — Freedom #6: Backing away
mappings.warning: This is procedural alignment, not a claim that the same mechanism is operating.

mappings.basis: Nova currently has no canonical action concept matching Gateway's cloud/fog/spray-outflow visualization and re-formation procedure.
mappings.warning: Do not force this unique imagery technique into a generic separation node merely for vocabulary completeness.

mappings.basis: Although the procedure has no NC action equivalent, its explicit Gateway purpose is separation/dissociation, which aligns with Décrochage as the target transition.
mappings.warning: No-equivalent procedure and shared target are not contradictory.

mappings.basis: The Floating method intentionally evokes floating/soaring sensations to support separation; Nova distinguishes Flottement as a cue/phenomenon from Décrochage as the transition.
mappings.warning: The crosswalk intentionally keeps cue and transition as two NC targets.
